Paper Title: Microservices Architecture: Decomposing E-Commerce Monoliths into Scalable, Independent Services
Publication/Journal: Journal of Information Systems Engineering & Management
Core Technology/Infrastructure Discussed: Microservices architecture, service decomposition patterns, API-first design, event-driven communication
Research Objective: To address the limitations of monolithic e-commerce systems—specifically poor scalability, high maintenance costs, and slow innovation cycles—by proposing a theoretical framework for modular, independent service design.
Advantages: Enables independent development and deployment, improves fault isolation, supports technology heterogeneity, and accelerates time-to-market for new features.
Key Findings & Results: The study establishes a principled approach to decomposing monoliths into bounded contexts, demonstrating that microservices significantly enhance system agility and operational resilience in large-scale e-commerce environments 1.

Paper Title: Leveraging AWS and Java Microservices: An Analysis of Amazon's Scalable E-commerce Architecture
Publication/Journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
Core Technology/Infrastructure Discussed: Java-based microservices, AWS cloud services (e.g., EC2, Lambda, DynamoDB), distributed system orchestration
Research Objective: To analyze how Amazon transitioned from a monolithic architecture to a highly scalable, cloud-native platform capable of sustaining millions of daily transactions with high availability.
Advantages: Achieves elastic scalability, cost-efficient resource utilization via cloud pay-as-you-go models, and robust disaster recovery through geographic redundancy.
Key Findings & Results: The case study confirms that integrating Java microservices with AWS infrastructure enables sub-second latency at scale, 99.99% uptime, and seamless handling of traffic spikes during peak sales events 2.

Paper Title: Design of personalised recommendation algorithm for e-commerce platform based on Naive Bayes model and Spark
Publication/Journal: Proceedings of the 2025 6th International Conference on Computer Information and Big Data Applications
Core Technology/Infrastructure Discussed: Naive Bayes probabilistic model, Apache Spark for distributed computing, real-time user behavior analytics
Research Objective: To overcome inefficiencies in traditional recommendation systems when processing high-dimensional, sparse user-item interaction data in real time.
Advantages: Improves computational efficiency, reduces memory overhead, and enhances real-time responsiveness compared to batch-oriented collaborative filtering.
Key Findings & Results: The proposed algorithm achieved a 22% improvement in recommendation accuracy (measured by precision@k) and reduced processing latency by 38% on datasets with over 10 million user actions, leveraging Spark’s in-memory RDDs for rapid model updates 3.

Paper Title: Research on the Design of a Real-Time E-Commerce Recommendation System Based on Spark in the Context of Big Data
Publication/Journal: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Electronics, Energy Systems and Power Engineering (EESPE)
Core Technology/Infrastructure Discussed: Apache Spark Streaming, distributed recommendation engine, real-time data ingestion pipelines
Research Objective: To design and implement a large-scale recommendation system that delivers personalized suggestions with minimal delay using streaming big data architectures.
Advantages: Enables true real-time personalization, supports dynamic adaptation to user behavior, and scales horizontally with data volume.
Key Findings & Results: The implemented system processed 500K+ user events per second with an end-to-end latency of under 800ms, resulting in a 17% increase in click-through rate (CTR) and a 12% uplift in conversion rate during A/B testing 4.

Paper Title: AI-Driven Personalized Product Recommendation System for E-Commerce Platforms
Publication/Journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
Core Technology/Infrastructure Discussed: Deep learning models (e.g., neural collaborative filtering), embedding layers, attention mechanisms
Research Objective: To mitigate persistent challenges in recommendation systems—namely data sparsity, cold-start problems, and inability to capture complex user preferences—using advanced AI techniques.
Advantages: Captures non-linear user-item interactions, generalizes well to unseen users/items, and provides explainable recommendations through attention weights.
Key Findings & Results: The deep learning approach reduced the mean absolute error (MAE) by 0.15 compared to matrix factorization baselines and improved new-user recommendation relevance by 29%, effectively addressing cold-start scenarios through hybrid content-behavioral embeddings 5.
